IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\n\nRafael Frias · Oct 15, 2026\nRepo: https://github.com/RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms · Site: https://rafaelfrias1.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/ · Tag: `mp2-final`\n\n## 1. What I built, and which grill decisions were mine\n\nI built a WordPress style CMS for the Kenyon Men's golf team as a hypothetical client. The admin and the editors would be the coach and the captain and team manager, respectively where they have different permissions (the captain and team manager can just make posts and edit their own while the coach can add/edit pages and also users). They all would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the GitHub Pages site to be viewed by readers within minutes. This was done with 7 tickets and 191 tests.\n\nThe grill decisions that were mine (went against the AI's recommendation) was adjusting the delete permissions to where only the admin could delete, going against what the client brief suggested (no one can delete past results). This allows for the coach to have final say/veto power over what is posted. Additionally, the AI suggested adding features that prevented the captain from posting qualifying scores (as was indicated in the client brief) however I overrode it since the small team and prospective audience made that unnecessary, as there is a significant level of trust between the captain and the coach that they will not overstep. I also ruled out features that were unnecessarily complicated for a first pass, like photo posting, search feature, and phone posting (even though the client brief said they post from a phone half the time).\n\n## 2. Where the AI drifted, and how the workflow caught it\n\nTicket 07 was built exactly to the ticket spec, and was passed by the reviewers without noticing the grader's copy would try to push to my repo, fail, and be blocked. This was caught when the run steps were checked against a fresh clone when running locally, so writing the README essentially forced us to look at it from a stranger's view. This catch resulted in commit fa985d3, which added a CMS_DEPLOY setting so only my laptop pushes to the site (recorded in ADR-004).\n\n## 3. Skills, prompts and resources, and why\n\nI first logged into WordPress to get a handle of what I was working on, and took note of what I found clunky, redundant, or what could maybe be improved upon. This was then used in the grill with docs session to generate actionable tickets.\n\nThe AI use statement in the README.md file shows the skills and prompts used. In addition, the final session used screenshots taken with Playwright for the submission requirements. This allowed me to ensure the screenshots were much more consistent to the project requirements rather than doing them by hand, which could leave room for mistakes.\n\nThe Matt Pocock skills came in super useful to catch inconsistencies and mistakes that I may not be as adept in catching as a novice developer. The AI questioning me on the documents provided allowed it to catch inconsistencies between the documents that would have presented problems when trying to implement the changes, and the code review caught mistakes I was able to question and change before committing, like the homepage saying \"Nothing published yet\" that the AI waved through.\n\nAdditionally, I went to bed after implementing tickets T01-T03 on the night of Oct 14, and used /handoff to ensure I could pick up where we left off the next morning and save tokens rather than having it reread the entire session again.\n\n## 4. Token budget: plan vs. actual\n\nPlan:\nSonnet 5.5 for /implement, and about 20% of a 5-hour window per ticket with 9 total tickets. Eventually taking up 2 and a half 5 hour windows.\n\nActual:\n8 tickets. T01-T06 used about 41% of a 5 hour window, and T07 about 13%. The T07 row in the ledger shows 40%, but that is because the phase label stayed on T07 while I did the screenshots, README, report and a mock grade afterwards. When taking into account grill (3%), setup (10%), and unlabelled sessions (9%), about 103% of a 5-hour window was used in the project spread across two main days (Oct 14 and 15), and about 1.8% of the weekly cap per ticket. This came in well under the forecast despite using Opus 5.5 instead. Likely came in under plan since opus remained efficient.\n\nMy first numbers were higher (116%) because the template's own sessions had been mixed into my ledger. The mock grade caught it, and I moved those rows out.\n\n## 5. Future improvements\n\nThe 403 page for editors is still a raw JSON instead of a friendly page, posts should be dated when they are published, not created, and the slug field only appears after first save, which could be tedious for an unfamiliar admin like a coach. These should all be improved before actual use of the site.\n\nAdditionally, the site still runs on placeholders for admin and editor, so real accounts should be created for the coach and captain, which would also solve the issue of the passwords being committed in the This was caught when the run steps were checked against a fresh clone when running locally, so writing the README essentially forced us to look at it from a stranger's view. This catch resulted in commit fa985d3, which added a CMS_DEPLOY setting so only my laptop pushes to the site (recorded in ADR-004).\n\n## 3. Skills, prompts and resources, and why\n\nI first logged into WordPress to get a handle of what I was working on, and took note of what I found clunky, redundant, or what could maybe be improved upon. This was then used in the grill with docs session to generate actionable tickets.\n\nThe AI use statement in the README.md file shows the skills and prompts used. In addition, the final session used screenshots taken with Playwright for the submission requirements. This allowed me to ensure the screenshots were much more consistent to the project requirements rather than doing them by hand, which could leave room for mistakes.\n\nThe Matt Pocock skills came in super useful to catch inconsistencies and mistakes that I may not be as adept in catching as a novice developer. The AI questioning me on the documents provided allowed it to catch inconsistencies between the documents that would have presented problems when trying to implement the changes, and the code review caught mistakes I was able to question and change before committing, like the homepage saying \"Nothing published yet\" that the AI waved through.\n\nAdditionally, I went to bed after implementing tickets T01-T03 on the night of Oct 14, and used /handoff to ensure I could pick up where we left off the next morning and save tokens rather than having it reread the entire session again.\n\n## 4. Token budget: plan vs. actual\n\nPlan:\nSonnet 5.5 for /implement, and about 20% of a 5-hour window per ticket with 9 total tickets. Eventually taking up 2 and a half 5 hour windows.\n\nActual:\n8 tickets. T01-T06 used about 41% of a 5 hour window, and T07 about 13%. The T07 row in the ledger shows 40%, but that is because the phase label stayed on T07 while I did the screenshots, README, report and a mock grade afterwards. When taking into account grill (3%), setup (10%), and unlabelled sessions (9%), about 103% of a 5-hour window was used in the project spread across two main days (Oct 14 and 15), and about 1.8% of the weekly cap per ticket. This came in well under the forecast despite using Opus 5.5 instead. Likely came in under plan since opus remained efficient.\n\nMy first numbers were higher (116%) because the template's own sessions had been mixed into my ledger. The mock grade caught it, and I moved those rows out.\n\n## 5. Future improvements\n\nThe 403 page for editors is still a raw JSON instead of a friendly page, posts should be dated when they are published, not created, and the slug field only appears after first save, which could be tedious for an unfamiliar admin like a coach. These should all be improved before actual use of the site.\n\nAdditionally, the site still runs on placeholders for admin and editor, so real accounts should be created for the coach and captain, which would also solve the issue of the passwords being committed in the transcript.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"serverClassifierContext":{"request":"f1744869-5574-477d-8428-c1e817a3116a","context":{"git_state":{"cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs","root":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","branch":"main","default_branch":null,"status":{"clean":false,"counts":{"staged":0,"modified":1,"untracked":null,"untracked_normal":1},"porcelain":null,"truncated":false},"visibility":{"origin":{"host":"github.com","remote":"RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"},"push_remote":"origin","remotes":[{"name":"origin","host":"github.com","remote":"RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}],"visibility_cache":[{"host":"github.com","remote":"RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}]}},"live_cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs","platform":"wsl"}},"sandboxed":false,"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"eccaa4ed-9fb3-4293-a3bc-8552f5860db3","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"classifier"},"session_id":"e68901dd-4f60-40d0-873c-0a5584ccf73d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"e68901dd-4f60-40d0-873c-0a5584ccf73d","version":"2.1.307","gitBranch":"main","slug":"see-the-manual-and-serene-candle"}

IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2: Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\n\nRafael Frias · Oct 15, 2026\nRepo: https://github.com/RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms · Site: https://rafaelfrias1.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/ · Tag: `mp2-final`\n\n## 1. What I built, and which grill decisions were mine\n\nI built a WordPress style CMS for the Kenyon Men's golf team as a hypothetical client. The admin and the editors would be the coach and the captain and team manager, respectively where they have different permissions (the captain and team manager can just make posts and edit their own while the coach can add/edit pages and also users). They all would access from a team laptop, and every change to the published content would update the GitHub Pages site to be viewed by readers within minutes. This was done with 7 tickets and 191 tests.\n\nThe grill decisions that were mine (went against the AI's recommendation) was adjusting the delete permissions to where only the admin could delete, going against what the client brief suggested (no one can delete past results). This allows for the coach to have final say/veto power over what is posted. Additionally, the AI suggested adding features that prevented the captain from posting qualifying scores (as was indicated in the client brief) however I overrode it since the small team and prospective audience made that unnecessary, as there is a significant level of trust between the captain and the coach that they will not overstep. I also ruled out features that were unnecessarily complicated for a first pass, like photo posting, search feature, and phone posting (even though the client brief said they post from a phone half the time).\n\n## 2. Where the AI drifted, and how the workflow caught it\n\nTicket 07 was built exactly to the ticket spec, and was passed by the reviewers without noticing the grader's copy would try to push to my repo, fail, and be blocked. This was caught when the run steps were checked against a fresh clone when running locally, so writing the README essentially forced us to look at it from a stranger's view. This catch resulted in commit fa985d3, which added a CMS_DEPLOY setting so only my laptop pushes to the site (recorded in ADR-004).\n\n## 3. Skills, prompts and resources, and why\n\nI first logged into WordPress to get a handle of what I was working on, and took note of what I found clunky, redundant, or what could maybe be improved upon. This was then used in the grill with docs session to generate actionable tickets.\n\nThe AI use statement in the README.md file shows the skills and prompts used. In addition, the final session used screenshots taken with Playwright for the submission requirements. This allowed me to ensure the screenshots were much more consistent to the project requirements rather than doing them by hand, which could leave room for mistakes.\n\nThe Matt Pocock skills came in super useful to catch inconsistencies and mistakes that I may not be as adept in catching as a novice developer. The AI questioning me on the documents provided allowed it to catch inconsistencies between the documents that would have presented problems when trying to implement the changes, and the code review caught mistakes I was able to question and change before committing, like the homepage saying \"Nothing published yet\" that the AI waved through.\n\nAdditionally, I went to bed after implementing tickets T01-T03 on the night of Oct 14, and used /handoff to ensure I could pick up where we left off the next morning and save tokens rather than having it reread the entire session again.\n\n## 4. Token budget: plan vs. actual\n\nPlan:\nSonnet 5.5 for /implement, and about 20% of a 5-hour window per ticket with 9 total tickets. Eventually taking up 2 and a half 5 hour windows.\n\nActual:\n8 tickets. T01-T06 used about 41% of a 5 hour window, and T07 about 13%. The T07 row in the ledger shows 40%, but that is because the phase label stayed on T07 while I did the screenshots, README, report and a mock grade afterwards. When taking into account grill (3%), setup (10%), and unlabelled sessions (9%), about 103% of a 5-hour window was used in the project spread across two main days (Oct 14 and 15), and about 1.8% of the weekly cap per ticket. This came in well under the forecast despite using Opus 5.5 instead. Likely came in under plan since opus remained efficient.\n\nMy first numbers were higher (116%) because the template's own sessions had been mixed into my ledger. The mock grade caught it, and I moved those rows out.\n\n## 5. Future improvements\n\nThe 403 page for editors is still a raw JSON instead of a friendly page, posts should be dated when they are published, not created, and the slug field only appears after first save, which could be tedious for an unfamiliar admin like a coach. These should all be improved before actual use of the site.\n\nAdditionally, the site still runs on placeholders for admin and editor, so real accounts should be created for the coach and captain, which would also solve the issue of the passwords being committed in the transcript.","is_error":false}]}}

{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"e68901dd-4f60-40d0-873c-0a5584ccf73d","hash":"5e19294292a04ffe2933394a03bdbc3e966b40a2f9966525a691678aad3ee59c","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01WZ1o9Tmc4mZFobR7nMjDqv","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/refiv/.claude/plans/see-the-manual-and-serene-candle.md","content":"# MP2plus plan: four exercises for the full +30\n\n## Context\nMP2plus (`docs/manual_iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_20261012.md`, rubric `docs/mp2plus-grading-rubric_20261012.md`) is an optional menu of 15 exercises. Points are added to the MP2 score, capped at **+30**. Only work after the tag `mp2plus-base` counts. The **gate**: every MP2 checker check and pytest test that passes at `mp2plus-base` must still pass at `mp2plus-final`, or every exercise scores 0. Grace ends **Wed Oct 21, 2:40 pm**. The judge reads the tag and email times from GitHub and the inbox.\n\nCurrent state: `mp2-final` = HEAD `3466c2a`. No `mp2plus-base` tag yet. `notes/usage-ledger.csv` has uncommitted changes. No MP2 feedback has arrived yet, so P1 carries a feature rather than a repair.\n\n## Chosen bundle: 33 points on the menu, +30 counted, 3 points of slack\n| Order | Exercise | Pts | Est. min | Why this one |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 0 | Part 0: tags, base checks, plan | 0 (required) | 15 | Without `mp2plus-base`, no exercise earns points |\n| 1 | **S2** Login hardening | 8 | 40–50 | Half of it is already done: `app/routes/auth.py:12-14` already gives one message and one status (401) for a wrong password and an unknown email |\n| 2 | **F8** Switchable theme, shipped **through P1** (branch + PR) | 7 + 6 | 75–90 | One change earns two exercises' points |\n| 3 | **P3** Decision record | 6 | 30–40 | No code. You write the three \"why\"s yourself |\n| 4 | **S1** Access matrix | 6 | 30–40 | `require_admin` (`app/web.py:75`) is already the single marker. It runs last, so it covers `/admin/settings` from F8 |\n| 5 | Part 2: report, tag, email | 0 (required) | 20 | Without the tag and email, no points |\n| | **Total** | **33** | **~3.5–4.5 h** | |\n\nP4 is left out: it depends on commit ordering and ledger labels and is easy to get wrong. If an exercise loses points, P3 or S1 can be swapped for it.\n\n## Steps\n\n### Part 0 (main)\n1. `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` and `uv run pytest -q`, recording the last line of each.\n2. `git tag mp2plus-base mp2-final && git push origin mp2plus-base`.\n3. Write `notes/mp2plus-plan.md` (exercises with minutes, base check results). Commit it as `mp2plus: plan` and push. Commit the ledger at the same time.\n4. `gh label create stretch` if the label is missing.\n\n### S2: Login hardening (phase `S2`)\n- Add an in-memory, account-keyed limiter next to `login()` in `app/routes/auth.py`: 5 failures per email in 15 minutes, then 429 or a lockout message even with the right password. The clock is passed in or injectable, and it uses only the standard library.\n- `tests/test_login_hardening.py`: same message and status for both bad cases; attempt 6 refused (frozen clock); login works again after 15 minutes; another email is not blocked.\n- `tests/conftest.py`: add an autouse fixture `reset_limiter`. **Only add lines; change none.**\n- Risk to the gate: an existing MP2 test may make more than 5 failed logins for one email. The autouse reset covers tests running one after another, so the full suite must be green before committing.\n- Commit `S2: ...`, push.\n\n### F8 through P1 (phase `T<issue#>`)\n1. Create the issue first: `gh issue create --label stretch --title \"MP2plus F8: Switchable theme\"`. Its body is F8's acceptance table, word for word, then `Blocked by: none`.\n2. `git switch -c mp2plus-theme`. Then:\n   - Move `CSS` out of `app/publish.py:36` into `app/themes/default/style.css`, and add `app/themes/<second>/style.css`. Each needs no horizontal overflow at 390 px.\n   - Add a `settings` table in `app/db.py`, plus an admin-only `/admin/settings` page (Depends `require_admin`, CSRF via `verify_csrf`, `url_for` links only).\n   - `render_site` (line ~135) writes the selected theme's CSS to `site/style.css`, which must always be written (`test_t00` depends on it).\n   - Tests go in `tests/test_theme.py` as `test_step2_…`, `step3`, `step4`, `step6`.\n   - Rebuild the database: `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`.\n3. Push the branch, then `gh pr create --body \"Closes #<n>\"`.\n4. Run `/code-review` and post the findings, with how each was resolved, **as a PR comment before the merge**. **Then push at least one more commit** (P1 row 4).\n5. `gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch` must close the issue.\n6. Save the screenshots `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-theme-1280.png` and `-390.png` (home page in the second theme, using the existing Playwright approach).\n\n### P3: Decision record (phase `P3`)\n- Add a **Decisions** table to `CONTEXT.md` with 3+ rows (question | choice | why). **The \"why\"s must be yours**: a client fact, a measurement, or a constraint, never a restatement of the choice. Candidates from the report: only the Coach deletes; `CMS_DEPLOY` gates the push; drafts never leave the database.\n- Add `docs/adr/ADR-006-<slug>.md` in ADR-002's format, naming a rejected option. Choose a decision the code shows (e.g. the theme stored in the database rather than `.env`, or the account-keyed limiter).\n- Commit `P3: ...`.\n\n### S1: Access matrix (phase `S1`)\n- Add `tests/test_access_matrix.py`. Walk `create_app().routes` and keep the routes whose dependant tree contains `require_admin`. That covers `/admin/accounts/*`, the pages routes (`app/routes/items.py:75`) and `/admin/settings`. Fill path parameters with seeded ids. The editor must get 403 or a redirect, and an anonymous client a redirect to `/login`.\n- Self-check: add a throwaway admin route, confirm the test picks it up, then delete the route.\n- Commit `S1: ...`.\n\n### Part 2\n- Write `docs/iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_report_rafael-frias_<YYYYMMDD>.md`, with one report row per exercise (S2, F8, P1, P3, S1) copied from the manual.\n- Re-run the checker and pytest. There must be no new failures.\n- `git tag mp2plus-final && git push origin mp2plus-final`.\n- Email the instructor with the subject `IPHS400 MP2plus - Rafael Frias`, the repo URL, the Pages URL and the tag, with the report attached.\n\n## What matters most for full points\n1. **The gate.** Never change an existing test line; only add. Run the full pytest before every push.\n2. **Order on GitHub.** The issue comes before the first push, and the review comment before the merge or close. Server times are what count.\n3. **Exact names.** `tests/test_theme.py` with `test_step<k>_…`, the screenshot file names, `/admin/settings`, `ADR-006`, the `reset_limiter` fixture.\n4. **A report row for every exercise.** An exercise without a row scores 0.\n5. **Set the phase before each exercise.** Commit prefixes: `S2:`, `T<issue#>:`, `P3:`, `S1:`. These follow the MP2plus manual and override the `T0N:` rule in CLAUDE.md.\n6. **Your own words** in P3's \"why\"s and nowhere generic. The judge scores the \"why\"s.\n\n## Verification\n- After each exercise: `uv run pytest -q` and `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2`. Both must be no worse than the base.\n- F8: `uv run cms publish`, then `diff site/style.css app/themes/<name>/style.css`. Switch the theme back, publish again and compare. Replay the settings POST without the CSRF token and expect 403.\n- S2: six bad logins in the browser, then the right password; expect the lockout.\n- S1: the throwaway-route check above.\n- Before tagging: `gh issue view <n>` shows CLOSED by the PR, and `gh pr view <n>` shows the review comment before the merge.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}

Write `notes/mp2plus-plan.md` (exercises with minutes, base check results). Commit it as `mp2plus: plan` and push. Commit the ledger at the same time.\n4. `gh label create stretch` if the label is missing.\n\n### S2: Login hardening (phase `S2`)\n- Add an in-memory, account-keyed limiter next to `login()` in `app/routes/auth.py`: 5 failures per email in 15 minutes, then 429 or a lockout message even with the right password. The clock is passed in or injectable, and it uses only the standard library.\n- `tests/test_login_hardening.py`: same message and status for both bad cases; attempt 6 refused (frozen clock); login works again after 15 minutes; another email is not blocked.\n- `tests/conftest.py`: add an autouse fixture `reset_limiter`. **Only add lines; change none.**\n- Risk to the gate: an existing MP2 test may make more than 5 failed logins for one email. The autouse reset covers tests running one after another, so the full suite must be green before committing.\n- Commit `S2: ...`, push.\n\n### F8 through P1 (phase `T<issue#>`)\n1. Create the issue first: `gh issue create --label stretch --title \"MP2plus F8: Switchable theme\"`. Its body is F8's acceptance table, word for word, then `Blocked by: none`.\n2. `git switch -c mp2plus-theme`. Then:\n   - Move `CSS` out of `app/publish.py:36` into `app/themes/default/style.css`, and add `app/themes/<second>/style.css`. Each needs no horizontal overflow at 390 px.\n   - Add a `settings` table in `app/db.py`, plus an admin-only `/admin/settings` page (Depends `require_admin`, CSRF via `verify_csrf`, `url_for` links only).\n   - `render_site` (line ~135) writes the selected theme's CSS to `site/style.css`, which must always be written (`test_t00` depends on it).\n   - Tests go in `tests/test_theme.py` as `test_step2_…`, `step3`, `step4`, `step6`.\n   - Rebuild the database: `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`.\n3. Push the branch, then `gh pr create --body \"Closes #<n>\"`.\n4. Run `/code-review` and post the findings, with how each was resolved, **as a PR comment before the merge**. **Then push at least one more commit** (P1 row 4).\n5. `gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch` must close the issue.\n6. Save the screenshots `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-theme-1280.png` and `-390.png` (home page in the second theme, using the existing Playwright approach).\n\n### P3: Decision record (phase `P3`)\n- Add a **Decisions** table to `CONTEXT.md` with 3+ rows (question | choice | why). **The \"why\"s must be yours**: a client fact, a measurement, or a constraint, never a restatement of the choice. Candidates from the report: only the Coach deletes; `CMS_DEPLOY` gates the push; drafts never leave the database.\n- Add `docs/adr/ADR-006-<slug>.md` in ADR-002's format, naming a rejected option. Walk `create_app().routes` and keep the routes whose dependant tree contains `require_admin`. That covers `/admin/accounts/*`, the pages routes (`app/routes/items.py:75`) and `/admin/settings`. Fill path parameters with seeded ids. The editor must get 403 or a redirect, and an anonymous client a redirect to `/login`.\n- Self-check: add a throwaway admin route, confirm the test picks it up, then delete the route.\n- Commit `S1: ...`.\n\n### Part 2\n- Write `docs/iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_report_rafael-frias_<YYYYMMDD>.md`, with one report row per exercise (S2, F8, P1, P3, S1) copied from the manual.\n- Re-run the checker and pytest. {"parentUuid":"7ab2fb5b-3148-421e-9f12-27af6ba3f5e4","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgGGfoFYitWBgKWfEy1FN","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Bb6FVp58fDCXtxnvaey9N6","name":"ExitPlanMode","input":{"plan":"# MP2plus plan: four exercises for the full +30\n\n## Context\nMP2plus (`docs/manual_iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_20261012.md`, rubric `docs/mp2plus-grading-rubric_20261012.md`) is an optional menu of 15 exercises. Points are added to the MP2 score, capped at **+30**. Only work after the tag `mp2plus-base` counts. The **gate**: every MP2 checker check and pytest test that passes at `mp2plus-base` must still pass at `mp2plus-final`, or every exercise scores 0. Grace ends **Wed Oct 21, 2:40 pm**. The judge reads the tag and email times from GitHub and the inbox.\n\nCurrent state: `mp2-final` = HEAD `3466c2a`. No `mp2plus-base` tag yet. `notes/usage-ledger.csv` has uncommitted changes. No MP2 feedback has arrived yet, so P1 carries a feature rather than a repair.\n\n## Chosen bundle: 33 points on the menu, +30 counted, 3 points of slack\n| Order | Exercise | Pts | Est. min | Why this one |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 0 | Part 0: tags, base checks, plan | 0 (required) | 15 | Without `mp2plus-base`, no exercise earns points |\n| 1 | **S2** Login hardening | 8 | 40–50 | Half of it is already done: `app/routes/auth.py:12-14` already gives one message and one status (401) for a wrong password and an unknown email |\n| 2 | **F8** Switchable theme, shipped **through P1** (branch + PR) | 7 + 6 | 75–90 | One change earns two exercises' points |\n| 3 | **P3** Decision record | 6 | 30–40 | No code. You write the three \"why\"s yourself |\n| 4 | **S1** Access matrix | 6 | 30–40 | `require_admin` (`app/web.py:75`) is already the single marker. It runs last, so it covers `/admin/settings` from F8 |\n| 5 | Part 2: report, tag, email | 0 (required) | 20 | Without the tag and email, no points |\n| | **Total** | **33** | **~3.5–4.5 h** | |\n\nP4 is left out: it depends on commit ordering and ledger labels and is easy to get wrong. If an exercise loses points, P3 or S1 can be swapped for it.\n\n## Steps\n\n### Part 0 (main)\n1. `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` and `uv run pytest -q`, recording the last line of each.\n2. `git tag mp2plus-base mp2-final && git push origin mp2plus-base`.\n3. Write `notes/mp2plus-plan.md` (exercises with minutes, base check results). Commit it as `mp2plus: plan` and push. Commit the ledger at the same time.\n4. `gh label create stretch` if the label is missing.\n\n### S2: Login hardening (phase `S2`)\n- Add an in-memory, account-keyed limiter next to `login()` in `app/routes/auth.py`: 5 failures per email in 15 minutes, then 429 or a lockout message even with the right password. The clock is passed in or injectable, and it uses only the standard library.\n- `tests/test_login_hardening.py`: same message and status for both bad cases; attempt 6 refused (frozen clock); login works again after 15 minutes; another email is not blocked.\n- `tests/conftest.py`: add an autouse fixture `reset_limiter`. **Only add lines; change none.**\n- Risk to the gate: an existing MP2 test may make more than 5 failed logins for one email. The autouse reset covers tests running one after another, so the full suite must be green before committing.\n- Commit `S2: ...`, push.\n\n### F8 through P1 (phase `T<issue#>`)\n1. Create the issue first: `gh issue create --label stretch --title \"MP2plus F8: Switchable theme\"`. Its body is F8's acceptance table, word for word, then `Blocked by: none`.\n2. `git switch -c mp2plus-theme`. Then:\n   - Move `CSS` out of `app/publish.py:36` into `app/themes/default/style.css`, and add `app/themes/<second>/style.css`. Each needs no horizontal overflow at 390 px.\n   - Add a `settings` table in `app/db.py`, plus an admin-only `/admin/settings` page (Depends `require_admin`, CSRF via `verify_csrf`, `url_for` links only).\n   - `render_site` (line ~135) writes the selected theme's CSS to `site/style.css`, which must always be written (`test_t00` depends on it).\n   - Tests go in `tests/test_theme.py` as `test_step2_…`, `step3`, `step4`, `step6`.\n   - Rebuild the database: `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`.\n3. Push the branch, then `gh pr create --body \"Closes #<n>\"`.\n4. Run `/code-review` and post the findings, with how each was resolved, **as a PR comment before the merge**. **Then push at least one more commit** (P1 row 4).\n5. `gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch` must close the issue.\n6. Save the screenshots `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-theme-1280.png` and `-390.png` (home page in the second theme, using the existing Playwright approach).\n\n### P3: Decision record (phase `P3`)\n- Add a **Decisions** table to `CONTEXT.md` with 3+ rows (question | choice | why). **The \"why\"s must be yours**: a client fact, a measurement, or a constraint, never a restatement of the choice. Candidates from the report: only the Coach deletes; `CMS_DEPLOY` gates the push; drafts never leave the database.\n- Add `docs/adr/ADR-006-<slug>.md` in ADR-002's format, naming a rejected option. Choose a decision the code shows (e.g. the theme stored in the database rather than `.env`, or the account-keyed limiter).\n- Commit `P3: ...`.\n\n### S1: Access matrix (phase `S1`)\n- Add `tests/test_access_matrix.py`. Walk `create_app().routes` and keep the routes whose dependant tree contains `require_admin`. That covers `/admin/accounts/*`, the pages routes (`app/routes/items.py:75`) and `/admin/settings`. Fill path parameters with seeded ids. The editor must get 403 or a redirect, and an anonymous client a redirect to `/login`.\n- Self-check: add a throwaway admin route, confirm the test picks it up, then delete the route.\n- Commit `S1: ...`.\n\n### Part 2\n- Write `docs/iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_report_rafael-frias_<YYYYMMDD>.md`, with one report row per exercise (S2, F8, P1, P3, S1) copied from the manual.\n- Re-run the checker and pytest. There must be no new failures.\n- `git tag mp2plus-final && git push origin mp2plus-final`.\n- Email the instructor with the subject `IPHS400 MP2plus - Rafael Frias`, the repo URL, the Pages URL and the tag, with the report attached.\n\n## What matters most for full points\n1. **The gate.** Never change an existing test line; only add. Run the full pytest before every push.\n2. **Order on GitHub.** The issue comes before the first push, and the review comment before the merge or close. Server times are what count.\n3. **Exact names.** `tests/test_theme.py` with `test_step<k>_…`, the screenshot file names, `/admin/settings`, `ADR-006`, the `reset_limiter` fixture.\n4. **A report row for every exercise.** An exercise without a row scores 0.\n5. **Set the phase before each exercise.** Commit prefixes: `S2:`, `T<issue#>:`, `P3:`, `S1:`. These follow the MP2plus manual and override the `T0N:` rule in CLAUDE.md.\n6. **Your own words** in P3's \"why\"s and nowhere generic. The judge scores the \"why\"s.\n\n## Verification\n- After each exercise: `uv run pytest -q` and `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2`. Both must be no worse than the base.\n- F8: `uv run cms publish`, then `diff site/style.css app/themes/<name>/style.css`. Switch the theme back, publish again and compare. Replay the settings POST without the CSRF token and expect 403.\n- S2: six bad logins in the browser, then the right password; expect the lockout.\n- S1: the throwaway-route check above.\n- Before tagging: `gh issue view <n>` shows CLOSED by the PR, and `gh pr view <n>` shows the review comment before the merge.\n","planFilePath":"/home/refiv/.claude/plans/see-the-manual-and-serene-candle.md"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":983,"cache_read_input_tokens":107660,"output_tokens":2470,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1364},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":983,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2470,"cache_read_input_tokens":107660,"cache_creation_input_tokens":983,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":983},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01Bb6FVp58fDCXtxnvaey9N6":{}},"serverClassifierRequest":"f565bfd8-3f4b-4bd7-8213-88eb5ab6e29d","apiBlockIndex":3,"requestId":"req_011CgGGfnygJn9J1vnG6NkfD","requestRef":"4e16e398-3e90-49d1-a914-a3f610b2f065","requestedModel":"claude-opus-5-5","type":"assistant","uuid":"b35131a0-ae86-481d-9276-f6d934ca95e7","timestamp":"2026-10-21T23:44:41.422Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"e68901dd-4f60-40d0-873c-0a5584ccf73d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"e68901dd-4f60-40d0-873c-0a5584ccf73d","version":"2.1.307","gitBranch":"main","slug":"see-the-manual-and-serene-candle"}

The autouse reset covers tests running one after another, so the full suite must be green before committing.\n- Commit `S2: ...`, push.\n\n### F8 through P1 (phase `T<issue#>`)\n1. Create the issue first: `gh issue create --label stretch --title \"MP2plus F8: Switchable theme\"`. Its body is F8's acceptance table, word for word, then `Blocked by: none`.\n2. `git switch -c mp2plus-theme`. Then:\n   - Move `CSS` out of `app/publish.py:36` into `app/themes/default/style.css`, and add `app/themes/<second>/style.css`. Each needs no horizontal overflow at 390 px.\n   - Add a `settings` table in `app/db.py`, plus an admin-only `/admin/settings` page (Depends `require_admin`, CSRF via `verify_csrf`, `url_for` links only).\n   - `render_site` (line ~135) writes the selected theme's CSS to `site/style.css`, which must always be written (`test_t00` depends on it).\n   - Tests go in `tests/test_theme.py` as `test_step2_…`, `step3`, `step4`, `step6`.\n   - Rebuild the database: `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`.\n3. Push the branch, then `gh pr create --body \"Closes #<n>\"`.\n4. Run `/code-review` and post the findings, with how each was resolved, **as a PR comment before the merge**. **Then push at least one more commit** (P1 row 4).\n5. `gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch` must close the issue.\n6. Save the screenshots `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-theme-1280.png` and `-390.png` (home page in the second theme, using the existing Playwright approach).\n\n### P3: Decision record (phase `P3`)\n- Add a **Decisions** table to `CONTEXT.md` with 3+ rows (question | choice | why). **The \"why\"s must be yours**: a client fact, a measurement, or a constraint, never a restatement of the choice. Candidates from the report: only the Coach deletes; `CMS_DEPLOY` gates the push; drafts never leave the database.\n- Add `docs/adr/ADR-006-<slug>.md` in ADR-002's format, naming a rejected option. Choose a decision the code shows (e.g. the theme stored in the database rather than `.env`, or the account-keyed limiter).\n- Commit `P3: ...`.\n\n### S1: Access matrix (phase `S1`)\n- Add `tests/test_access_matrix.py`. Walk `create_app().routes` and keep the routes whose dependant tree contains `require_admin`. That covers `/admin/accounts/*`, the pages routes (`app/routes/items.py:75`) and `/admin/settings`. Fill path parameters with seeded ids. The editor must get 403 or a redirect, and an anonymous client a redirect to `/login`.\n- Self-check: add a throwaway admin route, confirm the test picks it up, then delete the route.\n- Commit `S1: ...`.\n\n### Part 2\n- Write `docs/iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_report_rafael-frias_<YYYYMMDD>.md`, with one report row per exercise (S2, F8, P1, P3, S1) copied from the manual.\n- Re-run the checker and pytest. There must be no new failures.\n- `git tag mp2plus-final && git push origin mp2plus-final`.\n- Email the instructor with the subject `IPHS400 MP2plus - Rafael Frias`, the repo URL, the Pages URL and the tag, with the report attached.\n\n## What matters most for full points\n1. **The gate.** Never change an existing test line; only add. Run the full pytest before every push.\n2. **Order on GitHub.** The issue comes before the first push, and the review comment before the merge or close. Server times are what count.\n3. **Exact names.** `tests/test_theme.py` with `test_step<k>_…`, the screenshot file names, `/admin/settings`, `ADR-006`, the `reset_limiter` fixture.\n4. **A report row for every exercise.** An exercise without a row scores 0.\n5. **Set the phase before each exercise.** Commit prefixes: `S2:`, `T<issue#>:`, `P3:`, `S1:`. These follow the MP2plus manual and override the `T0N:` rule in CLAUDE.md.\n6. **Your own words** in P3's \"why\"s and nowhere generic. The judge scores the \"why\"s.\n\n## Verification\n- After each exercise: `uv run pytest -q` and `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2`. Both must be no worse than the base.\n- F8: `uv run cms publish`, then `diff site/style.css app/themes/<name>/style.css`. Switch the theme back, publish again and compare. Replay the settings POST without the CSRF token and expect 403.\n- S2: six bad logins in the browser, then the right password; expect the lockout.\n- S1: the throwaway-route check above.\n- Before tagging: `gh issue view <n>` shows CLOSED by the PR, and `gh pr view <n>` shows the review comment before the merge.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":18,"oldLines":6,"newStart":18,"newLines":20,"lines":[" "," P4 is left out: it depends on commit ordering and ledger labels and is easy to get wrong. {"parentUuid":"bdc25eb1-ff1e-4947-8c7c-dda58f4daeb3","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgGHDGu5DETXgisLZhbM2","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Part 0 is done and pushed, so MP2plus work can start.\n\n**Part 0:**\n- **Baseline checks:** the checker passed all 22 checks and all 212 tests pass. Nothing was already broken, so nothing gets set aside as a pre-existing failure.\n- **`mp2plus-base` tag:** it marks `mp2-final` (commit `3466c2a`) and is on GitHub. Only work after this tag is graded.\n- **`notes/mp2plus-plan.md`:** it lists the exercises with time estimates and the baseline results. It's committed as `mp2plus: plan` (`d05bb1d`) together with your usage ledger, and pushed.\n- **`stretch` label:** created on the repo, ready for the theme issue.\n\n**What you need to do:** pick exercises from a menu of 15. Your points are added to your MP2 score, up to +30. The plan reaches 33 so you have some slack:\n\n| Exercise | Points | Time |\n|---|---|---|\n| S2: login hardening (lock an account after 5 failed logins) | 8 | 40–50 min |\n| F8: switchable theme, shipped through a pull request (P1) | 7 + 6 | 75–90 min |\n| P3: decision record (a Decisions table in `CONTEXT.md` plus ADR-006) | 6 | 30–40 min |\n| S1: access-matrix test (editors and anonymous visitors are kept out of admin-only pages) | 6 | 30–40 min |\n| Report, `mp2plus-final` tag and email | 0, but required | 20 min |\n\n**Time:** about 4–5 hours in all, including a short grill session first.\n\n**What matters most for full points:**\n1. **Don't break anything that passes now.** If a check or test that passes today fails at the end, every exercise scores 0. Existing tests may only gain cases, never change.\n2. **Get the order right on GitHub.** GitHub's own timestamps decide this:\n   - Create the theme issue before you push any theme code.\n   - Post the `/code-review` findings, and how you resolved each, on the pull request before you merge it.\n   - Push one more commit after that comment.\n3. **Use the exact file and test names** the manual gives, e.g. `tests/test_theme.py` with tests named `test_step<k>_...`, and `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-theme-1280.png` and `-390.png`.\n4. **Give every exercise a row in the report.** An exercise without a row scores 0.\n5. **Write P3's reasons yourself,** as real facts or constraints. Generic reasons earn nothing.\n\n**The Matt Pocock skills** are installed, version 1.3.1. They aren't all in my skill list for this session, so type them yourself, e.g. `/grill-with-docs` and `/implement #N`.\n- `/grill-with-docs` is still worth a short session: it settles the theme and lockout choices, and your answers become P3's reasons.\n- The manual already supplies the spec and the issue text. Create the theme issue by hand with the manual's `gh issue create` command and its acceptance table pasted word for word. Don't let `/to-tickets` write that one.\n- Use `/implement` for the theme. For S2 and S1, the manual gives `/tdd` prompts instead.\n- Run `/code-review` before closing each exercise.\n\nYou said not to worry about lateness, so just one note: GitHub's push times show whether the final tag landed before today's 2:40 pm grace deadline.\n\n**Next:** `/clear`, run `echo grill > .claude/state/phase`, then start `/grill-with-docs`. {"parentUuid":"1ef3bd96-722a-4b8f-9244-3be705bdf8ac","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"69556a3d-1ae4-4d3e-ae1b-899c3ef961ff","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/refiv/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/ask-matt\n\n# Ask Matt\n\nYou don't remember every skill, so ask.\n\nA **flow** is a path through the skills. Most paths run along one **main flow**, and two **on-ramps** merge onto it. Everything else is standalone, or a vocabulary layer that runs underneath.\n\n## The main flow: idea → ship\n\nThe route most work travels. You have an idea and want it built.\n\n1. **`/grill-with-docs`** sharpens the idea by interview. Start here whenever you are **working in a working directory**: it's stateful, retaining what it learns in `CONTEXT.md` and ADRs. (No working directory? Use `/grill-me` instead, covered under Standalone. Both run the same `/grilling` primitive; `grill-with-docs` is the one that leaves a paper trail, which makes it the better of the two whenever a repo is there to leave it in.)\n2. **Branch: can you settle every question in conversation?** If a question needs a runnable answer (state, business logic, a UI you have to see), detour through a prototype, bridged by **`/handoff`** in both directions (a prototype lives in its own directory, which is exactly what `/handoff` is for; see Phase boundaries):\n   - **`/handoff`** out, then open a fresh session against that file,\n   - **`/prototype`** to answer the question with throwaway code,\n   - **`/handoff`** back what you learned, and reference it from the original idea thread.\n3. **Branch: is this a multi-session build?**\n   - **Yes** → **`/to-spec`** (turn the thread into a spec), then **`/to-tickets`** to split it into tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its **blocking edges**. On a local tracker that's one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature>/issues/`, worked blockers-first by hand; on a real tracker the edges become native blocking links, so any ticket whose blockers are done can be grabbed: kick off **`/implement`** per ticket, **`/clear`ing context between each one**. Each ticket is self-contained, so the last one's context is disposable.\n   - **No** → **`/implement`** right here, in the same context window.\n\n   Either way, **`/implement`** builds each issue by driving **`/tdd`** internally (one red-green slice at a time), then closes out by running **`/code-review`**, a two-axis review (Standards + Spec) of the diff, before committing. Reach for **`/tdd`** on its own when you just want to build a concrete behaviour test-first without a full spec, and **`/code-review`** on its own whenever you want to review a branch or PR against a fixed point.\n\n### Context hygiene\n\nKeep steps 1–3 in **one unbroken context window** (don't compact or clear until after `/to-tickets`) so the grilling, spec, and tickets all build on the same thinking. Each `/implement` then starts fresh, working from the ticket.\n\nThe limit on this is the **[smart zone](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/smart-zone)**: the window (~150k tokens on state-of-the-art models) within which the model still reasons sharply. If a session approaches it before `/to-tickets`, don't push on degraded; `/compact` at the nearest phase boundary and carry on (see Phase boundaries).\n\n## On-ramps\n\nA starting situation that generates work, then merges onto the main flow.\n\n- **Bugs and requests piling up** → **`/triage`**. It moves issues through triage roles and produces agent-ready issues, which **`/implement`** later picks up.\n\n  Triage is only for issues **you didn't create**: bug reports, incoming feature requests, anything that arrives raw. Tickets that `/to-tickets` produced are already agent-ready, so **don't triage them**.\n\n- **Something's broken** → **`/diagnosing-bugs`**. For the hard ones: the bug that resists a first glance, the intermittent flake, the regression that crept in between two known-good states. It refuses to theorise until it has a **tight feedback loop** (one command that already goes red on *this* bug), then fixes with a regression test. Its post-mortem hands off to **`/improve-codebase-architecture`** when the real finding is that there's no good seam to lock the bug down.\n\n- **A huge, foggy effort: a greenfield project or a huge feature build, too big for one session** → **`/wayfinder`**, the most cognitively demanding flow here. When the way from here to the destination isn't visible yet, it charts a **shared map** of **decision tickets** on the issue tracker and resolves them one at a time, producing **decisions, not deliverables**, until the fog is pushed back and the way is clear. Where **`/grill-with-docs`** sharpens an idea you can hold in one session, wayfinder is for the idea you can't, and it's slower and denser, so save it for exactly that, never a well-scoped feature.\n\n  When the map clears, **it hands off, it doesn't build**: merge onto the main flow at **`/to-spec`**, which collapses the map's linked decisions into a buildable plan, then `/to-tickets` and `/implement` as usual. Looping the map straight into `/implement` skips that collapse and throws the linked detail away, so go straight to `/implement` only when the effort turned out genuinely small.\n\n## Codebase health\n\nNot feature work, just upkeep.\n\n- **`/improve-codebase-architecture`** runs whenever you have a spare moment to keep the codebase good for agents to operate in. It surfaces **deepening opportunities**; picking one _generates an idea_ you can take into the main flow at `/grill-with-docs`. It's the survey that finds the candidates; **`/codebase-design`** (below) is the bench you design the chosen one on.\n\n## Vocabulary underneath\n\nTwo model-invoked references that run *beneath* the other skills, each the single source of truth for its vocabulary. Reach for them directly when the **words**, not the process, are the problem; or let the skills above pull them in.\n\n- **`/domain-modeling`**: sharpen the project's *domain* language: challenge a fuzzy term, resolve an overloaded word (\"account\" doing three jobs), record a hard-to-reverse decision as an ADR. It's the active discipline `/grill-with-docs` drives to keep `CONTEXT.md` a clean glossary.\n- **`/codebase-design`** is the deep-module vocabulary (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) for designing a module's *shape*: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface at a clean seam. `/tdd` and `/improve-codebase-architecture` both speak it.\n\n## Phase boundaries\n\nA **phase** is a chunk of work inside a session: the grilling, the implementation, the QA. At the **boundary** between two of them you have five options, and picking between them is the fuzziest decision in this whole map:\n\n- **Continue**: stay put. Costs nothing, loses nothing.\n- **`/clear`**: empty the window, when nothing here matters to what's next.\n- **`/handoff`** writes a portable markdown file. Narrow: only for a **new harness**, a **new directory**, a **colleague**, or forking a side task **mid-phase**. What it buys is portability.\n- **Subagent**: send a tightly-scoped task to its own window and get a report back.\n- **`/compact`** compresses this context and seeds a fresh session with it. The **default**, at the bottom of the tree rather than the first reach.\n\nRead [PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md](PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md) for the ordered tree: the five questions, the reasoning behind each branch, and why the primary-source cost makes **Continue** the one to rule out first. Make the decision **at** a boundary; mid-phase, continue or split the rest into subagents.\n\n## Standalone\n\nOff the main flow entirely.\n\n- **`/grill-me`**: the same relentless interview as `/grill-with-docs`, but **stateless**: it saves nothing locally and builds no `CONTEXT.md`. Reach for it when you are **not working in a working directory** (sharpening a plan, a design, a piece of writing, anything with no repo under it). If you are in a working directory, use `/grill-with-docs` instead: it runs the same interview and leaves a paper trail, so it is strictly the better one.\n- **`/grilling`** is the interview primitive itself: rounds, the frontier, facts are the agent's job and decisions are yours. `/grill-me` and `/grill-with-docs` are the two named ways in, and `/triage`, `/wayfinder` and `/improve-codebase-architecture` all run it internally. Reach for it directly only when you want the interview with no wrapper around it.\n- **`/resolving-merge-conflicts`** works an in-progress merge or rebase conflict hunk by hunk, resolving by **intent** traced to each side's primary source rather than by picking lines, then finishes the operation. It never runs `--abort`. Standalone and off every flow: reach for it when you are already mid-conflict.\n- **`/prototype`** is a small, throwaway program that answers one design question: does this state model feel right, or what should this UI look like. Throwaway is a constraint on how the code is written, not a promise to destroy it: the answer folds into the real code, and the prototype itself is kept as a **primary source** on a `prototype/<name>` branch out of main, pointed at from the implementation issue. It's the detour in step 2 of the main flow, but reach for it any time a design question is hard to settle on paper.\n- **`/research`**: delegate reading legwork to a **background agent**: it investigates a question against **primary sources**, then leaves a cited Markdown file in the repo. Keep working while it reads. The file it produces is something to take *into* the main flow at `/grill-with-docs`, since research feeds the thinking rather than replacing it.\n- **`/to-questionnaire`** comes in when the thing blocking you isn't in your head or the codebase but in **someone else's**, and it writes them a questionnaire to fill in. It's the inverse of `/grill-me`: instead of interviewing you about the subject, it interviews you about the **send** (who it's going to, what you need back) and aims the questions at the gap. What comes back is material for `/grill-with-docs` or `/to-spec`.\n- **`/wizard`** is for the steps only a **human** can take: provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, clicking through an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, running a one-off migration or cutover. It generates an interactive bash script that opens each URL, captures each value, and writes it into `.env` and GitHub secrets, so the procedure stops being something you re-explain to an agent every time. Model-invoked, so the agent reaches for it the moment it hits a wall only you can pass. If the agent could just do it itself, it should; this is for where a human is genuinely in the loop.\n- **`/wait-what`** is the corrective for a message that didn't land. Use it mid-conversation, inside any other skill, and the agent re-pitches what it just said with the context you were missing, in plain English, using the `CONTEXT.md` vocabulary. It works after the fact; `/grill-with-docs` is the upfront cure, because a shared language agreed early is what stops the jargon arriving at all.\n- **`/teach`**: learn a concept over multiple sessions, using the current directory as a stateful workspace.\n- **`/writing-for-agents`** is the reference for writing documents agents consume: skills, AGENTS.md, pointed-at docs.\n\n## Precondition\n\n**`/setup-matt-pocock-skills`**: run before your first engineering flow to configure the issue tracker, triage labels, and doc layout the other skills assume. Custom issue trackers also work.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: what should the next step be now"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"8fa52f4b-4d37-433a-946f-dc6114c2a7ac","timestamp":"2026-10-21T23:53:34.539Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"e68901dd-4f60-40d0-873c-0a5584ccf73d","version":"2.1.307","gitBranch":"main","slug":"see-the-manual-and-serene-candle"}

Model-invoked, so the agent reaches for it the moment it hits a wall only you can pass. If the agent could just do it itself, it should; this is for where a human is genuinely in the loop.\n- **`/wait-what`** is the corrective for a message that didn't land. Use it mid-conversation, inside any other skill, and the agent re-pitches what it just said with the context you were missing, in plain English, using the `CONTEXT.md` vocabulary. It works after the fact; `/grill-with-docs` is the upfront cure, because a shared language agreed early is what stops the jargon arriving at all.\n- **`/teach`**: learn a concept over multiple sessions, using the current directory as a stateful workspace.\n- **`/writing-for-agents`** is the reference for writing documents agents consume: skills, AGENTS.md, pointed-at docs.\n\n## Precondition\n\n**`/setup-matt-pocock-skills`**: run before your first engineering flow to configure the issue tracker, triage labels, and doc layout the other skills assume. Custom issue trackers also work.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: what should the next step be now"}]}}

{"parentUuid":"3da74125-1852-478f-a4a6-3d0985a0bb55","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgGHbCWFtTtRXLAbRRPYk","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Before you start, run `! echo grill > .claude/state/phase` and then `/clear`. Paste this as one message:\n\n```\n/grill-with-docs Get my repo ready for MP2plus, the extra-credit extension of my MP2 CMS. Grill me one question at a time on the decisions the assignment leaves open, then record the answers. Don't write any code in this session.\n\nRead these first:\n- @docs/manual_iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_20261012.md: sections S2, F8, P1, P3, S1, Part 2\n- @docs/mp2plus-grading-rubric_20261012.md: sections 2, 3, 4.1 F8, 4.2 P1/P3/S1/S2, 5\n- @notes/mp2plus-plan.md: my chosen exercises and baseline results\n- @CONTEXT.md: the glossary; use its words\n- @notes/client-brief.md: the client (Kenyon Men's Golf: Coach = admin, Captain/manager = editors)\n- @SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md: items #2 and #10\n- @docs/adr/ADR-002-stack.md: the ADR format to copy\n- @app/routes/auth.py, @app/web.py (require_admin, verify_csrf), @app/publish.py (the CSS string and render_site), @app/db.py\n\nMy exercises, in this required order:\n1. S2 Login hardening (phase S2, commit prefix \"S2:\")\n2. F8 Switchable theme, shipped through P1. The issue is created first, then branch mp2plus-theme, PR with \"Closes #N\", a /code-review findings comment on the PR before the merge, at least one commit pushed after that comment, then a merge that closes the issue (phase T<issue#>)\n3. P3 Decisions table in CONTEXT.md, plus docs/adr/ADR-006-<slug>.md (phase P3)\n4. S1 Access matrix generated from create_app().routes via require_admin. It goes last so it covers /admin/settings (phase S1)\n\nHard rules that are not up for debate (the acceptance tables are the contract):\n- The gate: the 212 existing tests and 22 checker checks must still pass. Existing test files may only gain lines. tests/conftest.py may only gain a fixture.\n- The F8 issue body is F8's acceptance table word for word, then \"Blocked by: none\", with the label \"stretch\". I create it by hand with gh, not /to-tickets.\n- Exact names: tests/test_login_hardening.py, tests/test_theme.py (test_step<k>_...), tests/test_access_matrix.py, docs/screenshots/mp2plus-theme-1280.png and -390.png, /admin/settings, app/themes/<name>/style.css.\n- Relative paths only, a CSRF token on every new form, no new dependencies, new settings go in .env.example, and a schema change means rebuilding cms.db with the seed script.\n\nGrill me on what is still open:\n- S2: 429 or a lockout message? Does a successful login reset the count? Is the limiter in memory or in the DB? How is the clock injected? What is the fixture called?\n- F8: the second theme's name and look, and why it fits the client. The default theme's folder name. Does the settings table store key/value pairs? Who sees the Settings link in the console nav?\n- P3: three Decisions rows. Ask me for each \"why\" and push back if my answer restates the choice instead of giving a client fact, a measurement or a constraint. Which decision is hardest to reverse (for ADR-006), and which option did I reject?\n- S1: how path parameters get filled, and what counts as \"redirected to login\".\n\nWhen we're done:\n- Add the new terms (Theme, Settings page, Lockout, ...) to CONTEXT.md.\n- Write the agreed P3 rows into CONTEXT.md as a Decisions table, in my words.\n- Draft ADR-006 for me to edit.\n- Give me a checklist of the session order. For each exercise, list: the phase to set, the issue or branch steps, the prompt to run, the review step, the commit prefix and the report row.\n- Then stop. Don't run /to-spec or /to-tickets until I say so.\n```\n\nWhy it's built this way:\n\n- **The `@` file references** load each document into the session, so the grill works from the actual assignment and code rather than its memory of them.\n- **The \"Hard rules\" block** keeps the grill from reopening things the rubric fixes. This conversation already holds both full assignment documents and our planning. Clearing it:\n- **Saves tokens:** without it, every grill turn re-sends all of that.\n- **Keeps the grill fresh:** it builds its own picture from the files you `@`-reference, which is how `/grill-with-docs` is meant to start.\n- **Keeps the grill, spec and tickets together:** after this clear, they all run in one unbroken window, which is what the Matt Pocock flow asks for.\n\nNothing is lost by clearing.
